Total ad spend is $136.98 across four campaigns. Free solo generated the best click efficiency at $4.41 per click. War room led in volume with 12 clicks. Deadline was paused after one day with zero spend.

War room clicks were 2, 4, and 4. It hit its daily cap on the third day at $19.94. Solo clicks were 2, 1, and 4. Its third-day spend was $15.94. Alter clicks were 2, 2, and 3. It spent $13.58 on the third day. Free solo improved to a $3.99 CPC on its third click.

War room can spend its full remaining budget. Solo and alter are under-spending their caps, leaving about $42 unused across the six days left. I will move more budget to war room while keeping solo for its strong efficiency.

Alter has roughly $28 left unused across the remaining days. Solo and alter totals should be trimmed to their realistic spend plus buffer. War room can absorb the freed budget. Solo is still the best converter and is accelerating, so cutting its budget now would be risky.

Each campaign has its own total budget, not a shared pool. Lowering solo or alter totals does not free spend for war room; the unused cap stays locked on those lines. To reach the full $550, I must raise war room's daily and total budgets while trimming solo and alter to keep the sum constant.

Solo could be trimmed to about $150 total. War room would then receive an extra $30 daily, raising its total budget to roughly $253. Deadline and alter totals would also drop to their realistic remaining spend plus buffer.

Final budget allocations are set. War room total is 240,000,000 and daily is 28,000,000. Solo total is 160,000,000 and daily is 19,000,000. Alter total is 140,000,000 and daily is 16,000,000. Deadline remains paused at 10,000,000. The remaining 182,000,000 will be spent evenly across the six days left.

War room has a slightly worse CPC than solo, but it is the only campaign with unused daily budget. Shifting spend there maximizes clicks and sign-ups. Audience expansion on solo and alter could raise volume, but it risks lowering lead quality and wasting money on irrelevant clicks.

Defined targeting will stay in place to avoid cheap clicks from unqualified audiences. A keyword ad group for Postgres and MySQL could reach database-specific traffic outside the software interest slice. That would require trimming another campaign's budget.

A new keyword line item will test Postgres, MySQL, and database traffic using the free solo post. It will pull $40 from war room's budget, lowering war to $220 total and solo to $150. The keyword campaign will run at $40 total with an $8 daily cap as a small pilot. Broad keywords will be combined with location and language targeting.

The keyword test will use the free solo post with broad targeting for postgres, mysql, and schema migration. It starts now and ends on November 30. The daily cap is $6 and the total is $40.

War room will keep its full budget. Solo and alter will each lose $10 and $30 respectively to fund the keyword test. Solo’s remaining daily budget is slightly higher than its projected spend, so it may clip at the end of the week.

The $40 keyword test leaves the total budget short by $7.50. War room will absorb that gap and its daily cap will rise to $23 to spend through the end of the week. The keyword test is being reduced to $25 so war room keeps more budget.

The keyword test is now set at $30 total with a $5 daily cap. War room will keep its full budget at $220 total and a $25 daily spend. Solo drops to $155 total and alter to $135. The weekly sum is exactly $550. If the keyword campaign performs poorly, it will be paused and its budget moved back to war room by Wednesday.
Line item 8yy2z is next. Targeting and promotion will be added. Other budgets will be updated. Then activation.
Pulling stats at noon on Wednesday, November 25.

Flight day 6 of 10 ends at 12:00 on Wednesday, November 25.

The war room campaign spent $100.81 with 42,107 impressions and 19 clicks at $5.31 CPC. Daily spend nears the $25 cap with 0.0451% CTR.

Free solo interest spent $64 on 38,415 impressions and 14 clicks at $4.57 CPC. Daily spend held steady near $14 with 0.0364% CTR.

Alter spent $61.59 on 30,847 impressions and 11 clicks at $5.60 CPC. Daily spend was $11.10 and $14.49 with 2 clicks each. Impressions collapsed from 6,329 to 1,510 on November 24 while spend rose.

Keywords free solo spent $9.39 on 9,252 impressions and 6 clicks at $1.56 CPC. Daily spend was $4.26 on November 23 and $3.47 on November 24. CPC is three times better than interest ads. It underspends the $5 daily budget. I will raise the daily and total budgets to test if this audience can absorb more.

The $5 daily cap is not the constraint; the campaign simply found less inventory. Broadening keywords should unlock more cheap clicks. I will add sql, dba, devops, schema, alter table, and database schema. These terms are wider than postgres and mysql but closer to the product than sql or devops.

I will raise the keywords free solo daily budget to $15 and total budget, pulling unused allowance from the alter campaign. Days left are 4.5 through November 30. War room has a small underspend versus its cap. Solo plan has roughly $28 unused.

Alter’s daily budget will drop to $12 and its total to $115, pulling $20 from other campaigns. The keywords free solo budget will rise to $12 daily and $50 total, using most of its $30 allowance. Deadline has spent $7.19.

The war room budget stays unchanged at $220 total and $25 daily. Free solo interest will not be cut because it is the best interest CPC and still underspends. Alter remains active rather than paused, since its $5.60 CPC is not far above war’s $5.31.

Solo and deadline budgets stay unchanged. I will add postgres migration and mysql migration to the keyword list alongside dba, schema migration, and alter table. I plan to review performance again on Friday at noon and possibly Saturday before the end. Reactivating the deadline post in the final 48 hours could tap into urgency.
The next check is Friday at 12:00. A final adjustment may be made before the weekend. The plan ends with a recap after midnight on November 30.
Two and a half days remain until the Black Friday deadline.

The combined Black Friday push runs through Friday, November 27 at noon.

War viff is the top spend at $151.83 with 28 clicks and a CPC of $5.42. Solo interest trails at $95.75 with 20 clicks and a CPC of $4.79. Alter vp65q has no clicks today despite 1,027 impressions and 5 engagements; it is the worst performer. Keywords are next.

Keywords is the most efficient campaign at $1.83 CPC. It spent $25.63 of its $50 cap, leaving roughly $7 unused over the remaining days. The daily spend is not consistently hitting the $12 limit.

Raising the daily budget to $15 would exhaust the remaining $24 before Sunday. The current $12 daily pace is sufficient to last through the end of the push. War viff has roughly $68 left of its $220 cap, but at the current $25 daily spend it will use about $62.50 over the remaining days, leaving only about $5.70 unused.

Solo interest has roughly $59 left of its $155 cap. At the current pace it will spend about $37.50 over the remaining days, leaving roughly $22 unused.

Alter vp65q has about $35 left of its $115 cap. It is losing money today with zero clicks and a rising CPC of $6.55.

Pausing Alter now would free up that budget. Keywords could absorb a small portion, but inventory is limited. Solo could spend more, but its total remaining budget exceeds what it will actually spend.

Solo’s unused budget is a total cap issue, not a daily limit problem. War is already spending its daily budget, so extra money can only go to War. The plan is to pause Alter and move its remaining budget into War. Alter’s total will be set to roughly $82 to cover in-flight spend, freeing about $33. That amount will increase War’s total budget to $253.

A $40 daily budget for War would be too aggressive. The rising CPC suggests the auction is pushing higher. War’s daily budget will rise to $35 and its total to $253 million.

War’s daily budget of $35 will leave roughly $13.70 unused over the remaining days, since its inventory may not support a higher spend. The keyword audience is the most efficient target, so the war room post could be promoted onto the keyword line item as well.

The war room post will be added to the keyword line item alongside the free solo post. The alter post is excluded because it is weaker. Keyword impressions are growing, so the audience is not exhausted. Running two posts may split the daily budget, but the first post could be fatiguing.

The combined budget cap of 550 remains intact after the reallocation. Alter’s total will be set to $85 million instead of $82 to cover any unbilled spend from today, giving War a $30 bump rather than $33.
A final check will run Saturday evening or Sunday morning to confirm nothing broke and budgets are intact. The campaign will close with a recap once the flight ends.
The Black Friday offer ends tonight at midnight.
